The turnover at the top of the security council could represent a balancing act by Ayatollah Khamenei “to prevent the excessive influence of Ghalibaf,” Azizi said.

Ghalibaf has in the past defended the cease-fire agreement that Iran struck with the United States in June, even as more hard-line elements within the country attacked the deal. 

Rezaei’s appointment, Azizi said, “would mean that the more hard-line side of the system is getting the upper hand.”

Saeid Golkar, a professor at the University of Tennessee at Chattanooga who studies Iran’s security forces, said Rezaei’s elevation was a further sign that the Revolutionary Guards were making the key decisions within Iran.

But in Golkar’s view, this change does not indicate that those decisions would be more hard-line, or more pragmatic for that matter.

What does seem likely, he said, is that Rezaei and Ghalibaf would eventually clash because of their intense ambitions. Like Rezaei, Ghalibaf has run for the presidency in the past. “This configuration is not going to work,” Golkar said. “Everybody wants to be a king.”

Officially, Iran’s president appoints the secretary of the council. In practice, however, the supreme leader decides who fills the post, Golkar said.

In videotaped comments shared widely on social media last week, Mohammad Bagher Kharrazi — a hard-line cleric related by marriage to Ayatollah Khamenei — anticipated the appointment and framed it as part of an effort to rein in Iran’s president, Pezeshkian. 

Pezeshkian and his foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, have been harshly attacked by Iranian hard-liners over their efforts at diplomacy with the United States.

In Kharrazi’s telling, Pezeshkian has repeatedly threatened to resign as president to get his way, and Ayatollah Khamenei, the supreme leader, has grown impatient and warned him he would accept his next such offer.

To further restrain the president, Ayatollah Khamenei was also working on changing the security council, planning to remove “Zolghadr and having Rezaei take his place,” Kharrazi said.

He also said that Ayatollah Khamenei had told Araghchi that “under no circumstances does he have the right to interfere in the negotiations anymore.”

Ayatollah Khamenei’s office, without naming Kharrazi, denied the account, as did Pezeshkian’s office.

📣 Brazil stablecoins face IMF scrutiny as crypto flows outpace capital 

🌐 IMF has called for closer oversight of Brazil’s stablecoin market as cross-border crypto flows outpace traditional capital movements. The report says cross-border crypto transactions have increased faster than conventional capital flows and now require closer regulatory attention because of their growing links with the country’s financial system. The assessment says stablecoin purchases respond much more strongly to global financial shocks than traditional portfolio investment or foreign direct investment. 

🔔 Based on the IMF’s analysis, purchases of dollar-backed stablecoins are two to three times more sensitive to external market events, raising concerns over how quickly international volatility could spread through crypto markets. Brazil has emerged as one of the world’s more active crypto markets, with stablecoins accounting for a significant share of digital asset activity. The IMF said the country’s crypto ecosystem has become increasingly connected with the traditional financial sector, making regulatory oversight more important as adoption continues to rise.

⚠️ The report acknowledges that Banco Central do Brasil (BCB) has already introduced measures to regulate crypto asset service providers. Even so, the IMF said several areas still need stronger rules, including customer asset protection, stablecoin issuance requirements, and compliance with anti-money laundering (AML) and counter-terrorist financing (CFT) standards.

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iran’s Foreign Ministry reiterates its commitment to close coordination with the Supreme National Security Council following the appointment of Mohsen Rezaei as the Council’s new secretary and representative of the Leader of the Islamic Revolution.

Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi conveyed his congratulations to Rezaei in a message on Monday, pointing to his years of experience in defense, security, and management fields as relevant to his new responsibilities.
​
Araghchi said Rezaei’s appointment as the top security official reflected confidence in his background and experience in dealing with complex strategic issues facing the country.
​
“This experience, under the current high-risk conditions and within a rapidly changing environment, is considered a valuable asset for fulfilling this important role,” Araghchi said in his message.
​
The foreign minister also underlined the importance of cooperation between diplomatic and security institutions.
​
“The Ministry of Foreign Affairs, as in the past, within the framework of the Islamic establishment’s overall policies and in close coordination with the Supreme National Security Council, will use all diplomatic capacities of the country to advance national interests, strengthen the authority of the Islamic Republic of Iran, and ensure and consolidate the country’s sustainable security,” he said.
​
Araghchi concluded his message by wishing Rezaei success in his new position and in efforts to serve the Iranian people and protect the country’s national interests.
